first.rationale: A guarded onboarding-simplification test addresses both declining completion and activation, with prior evidence of faster time-to-value and durable activation lift. The test should target self-serve accounts while retaining the full flow for complex-workspace accounts because prior shortening increased churn there. Promotional pricing is not preferred despite competitive pressure because its known 30-day retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the two simplification records to confirm treatment details, segment boundaries, and downstream outcomes before launch.

final.rationale: Run a segmented onboarding-simplification experiment for simple, self-serve SMB accounts only. The verified evidence directly addresses both current declines: shortened onboarding increased completion by 13% and reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, while SMB signup simplification increased activation by 9% and qualified revenue by 4%. Exclude complex-workspace accounts and preserve their full onboarding flow because shortening raised their 60-day churn by 9%. Measure qualified revenue and retention alongside completion and activation; do not assume results generalize beyond SMB or simple workspaces. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its known retention harm conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
